newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices fell to $93/T on good offers.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices fell to $93/T on good offers.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil market plunged $4 per tonne from Tuesday as unsold supplies continued to place pressure on prices, traders said on Wednesday.
Near market close, a 20,000 tonne cargo for lifting end February was traded at $93 per tonne.
"There were three to four sellers in the market chasing one buyer," said a trader.
Discussions were also heard that a handful of traders were interested in seeing lower prices. Sources said these players were "pricing out supplies".
The market has also started to move into a lull period ahead of the Chinese Lunar New Year holidays. "Nobody wants to take positions now," one trader said.
"Some Middle East cargoes are still heading this way but except for that the market is very quiet," he said.
China has covered its demand throughout February and was not seen buying in the near term, traders said.
"People are anticipating China to come out in March, but that does not mean it will buy in March," said another trader.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
